title: Calculus Volume 2
notes: OpenStax introductory calculus textbook covering integration, techniques, and applications. Digital ISBN-13: 978-1-947172-14-2; Hardcover ISBN-13: 978-1-938168-06-2.

title: Determining Volumes by Slicing
notes: Covers disk method and washer method (cross-sections perpendicular to axis of revolution, pp. 118-137).

title: Volumes of Revolution: Cylindrical Shells
notes: Comprehensive treatment of the cylindrical shells method for vertical, horizontal, and shifted axes of revolution, including comparison with slicing methods (pp. 137-152).

title: Rule: The Method of Cylindrical Shells
notes: Defines volume V = \int_a^b 2*pi*x*f(x) dx for continuous nonnegative f(x) revolved around the y-axis (p. 140, Rule 2.6).

title: Rule: The Method of Cylindrical Shells for Solids of Revolution around the x-axis
notes: Defines volume V = \int_c^d 2*pi*y*g(y) dy for continuous nonnegative g(y) revolved around the x-axis (p. 142).

title: Example 2.12: The Method of Cylindrical Shells 1
notes: Revolving y = 1/x over [1, 3] around the y-axis, yielding V = \int_1^3 2*pi*x*(1/x) dx = 4*pi (p. 140).

title: Example 2.13: The Method of Cylindrical Shells 2
notes: Revolving y = 2*x - x^2 over [0, 2] around the y-axis, yielding V = \int_0^2 2*pi*x*(2*x - x^2) dx = 8*pi/3 (p. 141).

title: Example 2.14: The Method of Cylindrical Shells for a Solid Revolved around the x-axis
notes: Revolving x = 2*sqrt(y) over [0, 4] around the x-axis, yielding V = \int_0^4 2*pi*y*(2*sqrt(y)) dy = 256*pi/5 (p. 142).

title: Example 2.15: A Region of Revolution Revolved around a Line
notes: Revolving y = x over [1, 2] around the line x = -1, yielding shell radius (x + 1) and V = \int_1^2 2*pi*(x + 1)*x dx = 23*pi/3 (pp. 142-144).

title: Example 2.16: A Region of Revolution Bounded by the Graphs of Two Functions
notes: Revolving region between y = sqrt(x) and y = 1/x over [1, 4] around the y-axis, yielding V = \int_1^4 2*pi*x*(sqrt(x) - 1/x) dx = 94*pi/5 (pp. 144-145).

title: Example 2.17: Selecting the Best Method
notes: Comparing disk vs. shell setup for region bounded by y = x, y = 2 - x, and x-axis revolved around y-axis (disks require 2 integrals, shells require 1 integral, pp. 145-147).
